elements.element: Services are performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.
elements.evidence: Section 19.1 expressly warrants that Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner by qualified personnel.

elements.element: Software and Deliverables materially conform to applicable documentation and agreed specifications.
elements.evidence: Sections 19.1 and 19.2 expressly require Deliverables to materially conform to their documentation and agreed specifications.

elements.element: The software/Deliverable conformance warranty lasts at least 12 months.
elements.evidence: Section 19.2 provides only a 90-day conformance period after acceptance. Section 19.1 contains no express 12-month duration, and the statement that Section 19.2 does not limit Section 19.1 does not affirmatively establish a 12-month continuing-conformance period.

elements.element: Services materially conform to applicable documentation and agreed specifications.
elements.evidence: Section 19.1 expressly warrants that Services will materially conform to their documentation and agreed specifications.

elements.element: The Services warranty lasts at least 90 days.
elements.evidence: No provision expressly provides a 90-day Services warranty period. Section 19.2's 90-day period applies only to each Deliverable, a term distinguished from Services in Section 19.1.

elements.element: Vendor must repair or re-perform a nonconforming item at no charge.
elements.evidence: Section 19.4 requires Vendor promptly to re-perform or repair the nonconforming item at no charge.

elements.element: Vendor must replace a nonconforming item at no charge.
elements.evidence: Section 19.4 requires Vendor promptly to replace the nonconforming item at no charge.

elements.element: A refund remedy is available if Vendor cannot timely cure the nonconformity.
elements.evidence: If Vendor cannot re-perform, repair, or replace within a reasonable period, Section 19.4 permits Customer to terminate the affected item and receive a refund of the Fees paid for it.

elements.element: Vendor and its performance of the Services comply with applicable laws.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause mentions industry standards, the Agreement, and Order Forms, but contains no express applicable-law compliance warranty.

elements.element: Software and Deliverables contain no malicious code.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no malicious-code warranty.

elements.element: The Services warranty lasts at least 30 days.
elements.evidence: The clause states no 30-day or other express duration for the Services warranty. The 90-day period in Section 19.2 applies to Deliverables, not Services, and preserving Section 19.1 does not supply the omitted Services duration.

result.reason: The redline supplies the fallback 90-day Deliverable period and the required cure and refund remedies, but it omits an express 30-day Services warranty duration, so fallback is incomplete notwithstanding the margin comment. Preferred also fails for lack of a 12-month software duration, applicable-law compliance, malicious-code protection, and a 90-day Services duration. The redline is not minimal because it changes the trigger from delivery to acceptance and adds wording beyond what was necessary while still failing to reach a complete level. It otherwise leaves unrelated terms effective, although the overlap between Sections 19.1 and 19.2 and the phrase “materially conform in all material respects” create avoidable ambiguity and redundancy.
